thumbnailAltText: The mild procedure addresses a major root cause of lumbar spinal stenosis (LSS) by removing excess ligament tissue to restore space in the spinal canal
jcr:description: The mild procedure addresses a major root cause of lumbar spinal stenosis (LSS) by removing excess ligament tissue to restore space in the spinal canal and does not significantly alter the structural anatomy of the spine.³ ⁴

text_copy_copy_copy_.text:
mild® addresses a major root cause of LSS1

Up to 85% of spinal canal narrowing is caused by thickened ligament. mild addresses this by removing excess ligament tissue using specialized tools and imaging.2,3

text_313900748_copy_.text:
A procedure with proven results4

With a 76.8% patient satisfaction rate,5 studies show that mild continues to improve patient functionality over time.6

text_copy_copy_copy_.text: Over one year, average standing time increased from 8 to 56 minutes with less pain7
Over one year, average walking distance increased from 246 to 3,956 feet with less pain7

Quick recovery time

Outpatient procedure and patients are typically discharged within 24 hours8

Safety profile

Similar to an epidural steroid injection4

Sedation

Can be performed using local anesthetic and sedation

Incision size 5.1mm9

Performed through a single incision; no implants used. Incision closed with a bandage

experiencefragment.text: Before, we used epidural steroid injections for lumbar spinal stenosis, but they only eased symptoms temporarily. With the mild procedure, we can now decompress the spinal canal by removing the ligamentum flavum to provide patients lasting relief* without changing the anatomy in a way that could affect future surgery. — Dr. Denis Patterson, DO (Pain Management Physician)
